name: Easter Island (Rapa Nui), Chile
clues: A thousand stone faces, alone in the blue, / we turned from the ocean to watch over you.
I have heads but no thoughts, and many of my bodies are buried deep underground. My island is the most remote place people live in the Pacific. What am I?
Giant carved heads called moai. Part of Chile, deep in the Pacific.
fact: Most moai face inland, watching over the villages that carved them.

name: Hermitage Museum, St Petersburg, Russia
clues: My halls hold three million treasures in all, / and cats chase the mice that run under my hall.
I'm a palace that became a house of paintings, and my winter home sits on a river that freezes. What am I?
A giant art museum on the Neva River.
fact: The Hermitage was founded by Catherine the Great in 1764.

name: Taipei 101, Taiwan
clues: I'm built like bamboo, in segments I rise, / a giant gold ball keeps me calm in the skies.
My name is a number, and each New Year I shoot fireworks from my sides. What am I?
A skyscraper in Taiwan's capital.
fact: Taipei 101 was the tallest building in the world from 2004 to 2010.

name: Plitvice Lakes, Croatia
clues: Sixteen blue lakes on a staircase of trees, / spilling in waterfalls just as they please.
My dams were built by no beaver or engineer, and they keep growing every year. What am I?
A national park of terraced lakes in Croatia.
fact: The lakes are separated by natural dams of travertine that are still growing.

name: Okavango Delta, Botswana
clues: In the dry season my waters arrive, / and elephants splash where the desert should thrive.
I'm a river that never reaches the sea. I end in a swamp full of hippos instead. What am I?
A giant inland delta in Botswana.
fact: The Okavango floods at the height of the dry season, because the rain falls months earlier in Angola.

name: Matterhorn, Switzerland and Italy
clues: A crooked tooth biting the sky, I stand, / on a chocolate bar, I'm the shape of the brand.
I'm a pyramid that no pharaoh built, shared by two countries above a car-free town. What am I?
A pyramid-shaped peak above Zermatt.
fact: The Matterhorn was first climbed in 1865 by Edward Whymper's team.

name: Meteora, Greece
clues: We pray in the clouds on our pillars of stone, / once reached by a basket and rope alone.
My name means suspended in the air, though I've never flown. What am I?
Monasteries on top of rock pillars in central Greece.
fact: Six of Meteora's monasteries are still active today.

name: Chichen Itza, Mexico
clues: Count all my steps and a year you will find, / clap at my base and a bird calls behind.
Twice a year a serpent of shadow slithers down my staircase, yet no snake is there. What am I?
The great Maya pyramid of El Castillo in the Yucatán.
fact: El Castillo has 91 steps on each of its four sides, plus the top platform, for 365 in all.

name: Golden Gate Bridge, San Francisco, USA
clues: I'm not made of gold though my name tells you so, / I stretch through the fog where the big ships go.
I'm painted International Orange, and my painters never really stop. What am I?
A red-orange suspension bridge across a Californian strait.
fact: When it opened in 1937, the Golden Gate had the longest main span of any suspension bridge in the world.

name: Charles Bridge, Prague, Czechia
clues: Thirty saints line me from tower to tower, / rub one for luck and wish with all your power.
My builders said they mixed egg yolks into my mortar, and a king laid my first stone at a lucky time. What am I?
A medieval stone bridge over the Vltava River.
fact: Construction of Charles Bridge began in 1357.

name: Cliffs of Moher, Ireland
clues: Seven hundred feet of rock face the west, / where puffins and waves do battle and rest.
I'm a wall with no house behind it, starring as the Cliffs of Insanity in a famous film. What am I?
Famous sea cliffs in County Clare, Ireland.
fact: The Cliffs of Moher stretch for about 14 km.

name: Giant's Causeway, Northern Ireland
clues: A giant built stepping stones over the sea, / or lava cooled hexagons, take it from me.
Forty thousand stones stand here like a honeycomb road, and legend says it leads to Scotland. What am I?
Basalt columns on the coast of County Antrim.
fact: The columns formed about 60 million years ago when lava cooled and cracked.

name: Baikonur Cosmodrome, Kazakhstan
clues: From my flat steppe the first human flew high, / I'm rented to send people into the sky.
I'm in one country but leased by another, and every rocket I launch goes up near camels. What am I?
The world's first and largest spaceport, on the Kazakh steppe.
fact: Yuri Gagarin launched from Baikonur on 12 April 1961.

name: Machu Picchu, Peru
clues: A lost city hidden on a mountain's high crown, / the Spanish rode past and never looked down.
I was built without mortar, and llamas trim my lawn. What am I?
The Inca citadel in the Andes of Peru.
fact: Machu Picchu was built in the 1400s, likely as an estate for the Inca emperor Pachacuti.

name: Iguazu Falls, Argentina and Brazil
clues: A first lady once said, as she looked at my face, / poor Niagara! I'm in a much bigger place.
I'm one waterfall made of almost 300, and my deepest drop is called the Devil's Throat. What am I?
Giant waterfalls on the Argentina and Brazil border.
fact: Iguazu is made of about 275 separate waterfalls spread over nearly 3 km.

name: Milford Sound, New Zealand
clues: When rain starts to fall, my cliffs come alive, / with a thousand new waterfalls taking a dive.
I'm called a sound, but I'm really a fjord, and I'm one of the wettest places people visit. What am I?
A deep fjord in the far southwest of New Zealand's South Island.
fact: Milford Sound gets about 6.8 m of rain a year, making it one of the wettest places on Earth.

name: Golden Temple, Amritsar, India
clues: My roof is of gold and my kitchen is free, / a hundred thousand are fed here by me.
I float on a lake of nectar, and my four doors welcome people of every faith. What am I?
The holiest shrine of Sikhism, covered in gold.
fact: Anyone can eat at the Golden Temple's langar, whatever their religion.

name: Serengeti, Tanzania
clues: A million hooves thunder in circles each year, / the plain without end is the meaning here.
My name means endless plains, and the biggest traffic jam on my roads is made of wildebeest. What am I?
A famous savanna national park in Tanzania.
fact: The great migration includes about 1.5 million wildebeest plus hundreds of thousands of zebras.

name: Twelve Apostles, Australia
clues: They called us the Apostles, though twelve we were not, / and the waves keep on taking the few that we've got.
We're named after twelve, but there were never that many of us, and the sea keeps knocking us down. What am I?
Limestone stacks along the Great Ocean Road.
fact: The cliffs here retreat about 2 cm a year.

name: Great Pyramid of Giza, Egypt
clues: I once wore white like a mirror of sun, / for nearly four thousand years, the tallest one.
I'm the oldest of the Seven Wonders, and the only one still standing. What am I?
The great pyramids just outside Cairo.
fact: The Great Pyramid was originally covered in polished white limestone that made it shine in the sun.

name: Pamukkale, Turkey
clues: I look like a hillside of fresh fallen snow, / but warm water flows where the white terraces glow.
My name means cotton castle, and you must take off your shoes to climb me. What am I?
Pamukkale, in southwestern Turkey.
fact: Visitors to Pamukkale must walk the terraces barefoot to protect the soft travertine.

name: Uluru, Australia
clues: I glow like an ember when daylight is new, / a red island rising in desert's hue.
I'm a rock that changes color through the day, and most of me is hidden underground. What am I?
Uluru, also called Ayers Rock.
fact: Uluru is about 348 m high and 9.4 km around at its base.

name: Bran Castle, Romania
clues: A count with sharp teeth made my castle well known, / though he never existed and slept here alone.
I'm famous for a vampire who never lived here, written by an author who never visited me. What am I?
A castle in the Carpathians near Brașov.
fact: Bram Stoker never visited Romania.

name: Stonehenge, England
clues: Stones from far Wales were dragged to my plain, / I tell the year's turning by sun, not by rain.
I'm a calendar you can walk around, and no one knows for sure who built me. What am I?
Stonehenge, on Salisbury Plain.
fact: Stonehenge's biggest stones, the sarsens, weigh around 25 tonnes each.

name: Stone Town, Zanzibar, Tanzania
clues: Carved wooden doors and the scent of cloves, / an island of spice where the dhow boat roves.
A rock legend was born on my island, and the shortest war in history was fought here. What am I?
The old town of a spice island off Tanzania.
fact: Zanzibar was famous for cloves and was once the world's largest producer.

name: Reine, Lofoten, Norway
clues: Red cabins on stilts where the cod fish hang dry, / under peaks and the dancing green lights of the sky.
I'm a fishing village above the Arctic Circle that stays mild in winter. What am I?
A fishing village in the Lofoten Islands.
fact: Lofoten is far north of the Arctic Circle but has a mild climate thanks to the Gulf Stream.

name: Pripyat and Chernobyl, Ukraine
clues: My Ferris wheel never turned for a ride, / the forest moved in when the people moved outside.
I'm a city frozen in 1986, guarded by a giant steel arch. What am I?
The abandoned city next to the Chernobyl nuclear plant.
fact: The New Safe Confinement arch over Chernobyl's reactor is one of the largest movable structures ever built.

name: St Peter's Basilica, Vatican City
clues: My dome looks down on a country so small, / the whole of it fits within one city wall.
I'm the largest church in the smallest country, built over a fisherman's grave. What am I?
The great church of the Pope.
fact: Vatican City covers just 0.44 square kilometers.

name: Kīlauea, Hawaii, USA
clues: I'm home to a goddess with hair made of glass, / I build brand new land each time that I pass.
I'm one of the most active volcanoes on Earth, and I make my island bigger. What am I?
A volcano on Hawaii's Big Island.
fact: Kīlauea erupted almost continuously from 1983 to 2018.

name: Venice, Italy
clues: My streets are of water, my taxis are boats, / I'm sinking a little, but still stay afloat.
I stand on a forest you'll never see, upside down under the water. What am I?
The Italian city of gondolas and canals.
fact: The wooden piles under Venice have lasted centuries because, without oxygen underwater, they slowly turned almost to stone.

name: Great Blue Hole, Belize
clues: A sapphire eye in the turquoise sea, / divers fall into the deep blue of me.
I'm a hole that you can see from space, and I'm full of water and sharks. What am I?
The Great Blue Hole, off the coast of Belize.
fact: The Great Blue Hole is about 300 m across and 125 m deep.

name: Acropolis, Athens, Greece
clues: Up on my rock stands a temple of white, / built for the goddess of wisdom and fight.
My most famous building has no straight lines, though it looks perfectly straight. What am I?
The rock above Athens, crowned by the Parthenon.
fact: The Parthenon was finished in 432 BC and dedicated to the goddess Athena.

name: Mont-Saint-Michel, France
clues: Twice every day I'm an island at sea, / then the tide rushes out and you walk up to me.
I'm an abbey on a rock that is sometimes surrounded by sand and sometimes by water. What am I?
A tidal island abbey off the coast of Normandy.
fact: The tides around Mont-Saint-Michel are among the strongest in Europe, up to 14 m.

name: Zhangjiajie, China
clues: Stone towers float in the mist like a dream, / a film about blue aliens borrowed my theme.
Thousands of sandstone pillars rise here, and a glass bridge lets visitors walk across the sky. What am I?
A forest park of stone towers in Hunan.
fact: One pillar was renamed 'Avatar Hallelujah Mountain' in 2010.

name: Old Faithful, Yellowstone, USA
clues: I'm not the biggest, but true to my name, / I blow off my steam like a clockwork game.
I keep a schedule better than most trains, and rangers can predict my next burst. What am I?
The famous geyser in the world's first national park.
fact: Old Faithful erupts roughly every 60 to 110 minutes.

name: Terracotta Army, Xi'an, China
clues: Eight thousand soldiers stand silent in clay, / waiting to fight for an emperor one day.
We're an army that has never fought. Farmers found us while digging a well. What am I?
Clay warriors guarding China's first emperor.
fact: About 8,000 soldiers, 130 chariots and 670 horses are thought to be buried there.

name: Varanasi, India
clues: I'm older than legends, my fires burn bright, / on steps by a river by day and by night.
Pilgrims come here to bathe at dawn, and some come here to end their lives' journey. What am I?
One of the oldest living cities, on the Ganges.
fact: Varanasi has more than 80 ghats along the Ganges.

name: Sossusvlei, Namibia
clues: Dunes red as rust and trees dead as stone, / the oldest desert has a valley alone.
My trees died 900 years ago but are still standing, because it's too dry for them to rot. What am I?
Red sand dunes in the Namib Desert.
fact: The Namib is often called the oldest desert in the world, at around 55 million years.

name: Bagan, Myanmar
clues: Ten thousand temples once rose from my plain, / balloons drift at dawn above all that remain.
I'm a plain of thousands of temples, and my kings built them over just a few centuries. What am I?
An ancient temple city on the Irrawaddy River in Myanmar.
fact: Over 10,000 temples were built at Bagan between the 11th and 13th centuries.

name: Taj Mahal, India
clues: A tomb made of love in marble so white, / I blush in the morning and gleam in moonlight.
An emperor built me for his favorite wife, and my towers lean out on purpose. What am I?
The Taj Mahal in Agra.
fact: The four minarets of the Taj Mahal lean slightly outward so they would fall away from the tomb in an earthquake.

name: Statue of Liberty, New York, USA
clues: I came here in crates, and my copper turned green, / the tallest welcome a ship's ever seen.
I came from France in pieces, and I turned green after I arrived. What am I?
A torch-bearing gift from France in New York Harbor.
fact: The Statue of Liberty's index finger is about 2.4 m long.

name: Gorée Island, Senegal
clues: Pink houses and flowers hide what I've known, / a door that looks out to the sea, all alone.
I'm a small island with no cars, and my most visited door faces the ocean and has no return. What am I?
A small island off Dakar, Senegal.
fact: Gorée became one of UNESCO's first World Heritage Sites in 1978.

name: Lake Natron, Tanzania
clues: Flamingos are born on my blood-red brine, / but what falls in my water turns stone over time.
I'm a lake so salty and hot that animals that die in me look like statues. What am I?
A red soda lake in northern Tanzania.
fact: Lake Natron's red color comes from tiny salt-loving microorganisms.

name: Mount Kilimanjaro, Tanzania
clues: Snow on my crown though I stand near the line / where the sun shines the hottest, the Earth's middle sign.
I'm the tallest mountain that stands alone, and you can hike to my top without ropes. What am I?
Africa's highest peak, in Tanzania.
fact: Kilimanjaro's summit, Uhuru Peak, is 5,895 m above sea level.

name: Hollywood Sign, Los Angeles, USA
clues: My letters are giants, but I'm not a word / you'll find in a dictionary, so I've heard.
I used to have four more letters, and I'm the most famous sign in the world. What am I?
White letters on a hillside above Los Angeles.
fact: The sign originally read HOLLYWOODLAND. The last four letters were removed in 1949.

name: Wadi Rum, Jordan
clues: My red sands played Mars in a film or two, / and a famous Lawrence once rode right through.
I've been Mars in the movies, and I'm called the Valley of the Moon. What am I?
The Valley of the Moon desert in southern Jordan.
fact: Wadi Rum has stood in for Mars in films like The Martian.

name: Tristan da Cunha
clues: No airport, no runway, just ocean and foam, / the loneliest island that people call home.
My nearest neighbor is about 2,400 km away, and I'm reached only by a week at sea. What am I?
A volcanic island in the middle of the South Atlantic.
fact: Tristan da Cunha has no airport. It takes about a week by boat from South Africa.

name: Chocolate Hills, Bohol, Philippines
clues: A thousand green hills, each shaped like a cone, / turn brown in the dry months, like sweets of their own.
I'm named after a treat, but you can't eat me. What am I?
Cone-shaped hills on Bohol island.
fact: There are at least 1,260 Chocolate Hills.

name: Lake Baikal, Russia
clues: So deep and so old and so clear you can see, / a fifth of Earth's unfrozen fresh water's in me.
I'm the deepest lake on Earth, and seals live in me, far from any ocean. What am I?
Lake Baikal.
fact: Lake Baikal is about 25 million years old and more than 1,600 m deep.

name: Nazca Lines, Peru
clues: A monkey, a spider, a bird drawn in sand, / only from the sky can you see them as planned.
My drawings are so big that they make sense only from the air, and they've lasted because it never rains here. What am I?
Giant desert drawings in southern Peru.
fact: The lines have survived so long because the area gets almost no rain or wind.

name: Petra, Jordan
clues: Rose-red and carved from the face of a cliff, / my treasury holds nothing but stone, if you sniff.
My most famous building has a front but no back, and most of my city is still buried. What am I?
The ancient Nabataean city of Petra.
fact: Scientists estimate that around 85% of Petra is still buried and unexcavated.

name: Great Wall of China (Badaling)
clues: I'm a dragon of stone, made of bricks and of rice, / I curl over mountains, and climbing me's nice.
People say astronauts can see me from space, but they can't. Still, I'm the longest thing humans ever built. What am I?
The Great Wall of China, at Badaling near Beijing.
fact: All the sections of the Great Wall added together stretch about 21,000 km.

name: Mount Bromo, Indonesia
clues: Smoke from my crater, a sea made of sand, / at dawn tourists shiver to see where I stand.
Every year people climb my rim and throw offerings into my smoking mouth. What am I?
An active volcano in East Java.
fact: The Tenggerese people hold the Yadnya Kasada festival at Bromo every year.

name: Bora Bora, French Polynesia
clues: Huts on stilts where the lagoon glows bright, / green peak in the middle, turquoise in sight.
I'm an island wrapped in a ring of reef, and my most famous bedrooms stand over water. What am I?
An island in French Polynesia.
fact: Overwater bungalows were invented in French Polynesia in the 1960s.

name: Lake Hillier, Australia
clues: Pink as a milkshake beside the blue sea, / I'm salty, not sweet, so don't drink from me.
I'm a lake that looks like bubble gum from the air, and I stay pink even in a glass. What am I?
A pink lake on an island off Western Australia.
fact: Lake Hillier's color comes from salt-loving algae and microbes.

name: Victoria Peak, Hong Kong
clues: A tram climbs so steep the buildings seem to lean, / up to the best view of a skyscraper scene.
I'm a hilltop above the city with the most skyscrapers on Earth. What am I?
The highest hill on Hong Kong Island.
fact: Hong Kong has more skyscrapers than any other city in the world.

name: Rock of Gibraltar
clues: A lion of limestone that guards the sea's door, / wild monkeys steal sandwiches up on my floor.
I'm one of the Pillars of Hercules, and planes cross a busy road to land beside me. What am I?
A British limestone rock at the tip of Spain.
fact: About 300 Barbary macaques live on the Rock of Gibraltar.

name: Leaning Tower of Pisa, Italy
clues: I've tilted for centuries, still I don't fall, / tourists pretend to hold up my wall.
My builders made a mistake that turned me into a star, and engineers worked hard to fix me just a little. What am I?
A tilted bell tower in Tuscany.
fact: The tower took about 200 years to build, partly because wars kept stopping the work.

name: Darvaza Gas Crater, Turkmenistan
clues: A hole full of fire that will never burn out, / the Door to Hell is what locals shout.
Scientists set me on fire to burn off gas in a few days. Decades later, I'm still burning. What am I?
A burning crater in the Karakum Desert.
fact: The crater is about 70 m wide and has been burning for decades.

name: Edinburgh Castle, Scotland
clues: On an old volcano my towers are set, / a gun fires at one so no ship will forget.
I sit on top of an extinct volcano, and every day but Sunday, a cannon tells the time. What am I?
The castle on the rock above Scotland's capital.
fact: The One O'Clock Gun has been fired since 1861 so ships could set their clocks.

name: Christ the Redeemer, Rio de Janeiro
clues: My arms open wide on a mountain so high, / I watch over beaches and samba nearby.
I'm struck by lightning several times a year, but I keep my arms open. What am I?
The Christ the Redeemer statue in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil.
fact: Christ the Redeemer was finished in 1931 and is about 30 m tall, not counting its pedestal.

name: Sagrada Família, Barcelona, Spain
clues: A forest of stone where the columns are trees, / and cranes keep on working as long as they please.
I've been under construction since the 1880s, and my architect is buried inside me. What am I?
Gaudí's giant basilica in Barcelona.
fact: Antoni Gaudí worked on the Sagrada Família for more than 40 years, until his death in 1926.

name: Panmunjom, Korean DMZ
clues: Blue huts on a border where soldiers stand guard, / step over a line, and the step can be hard.
I'm a village where two countries still technically at war meet across a concrete line. What am I?
The truce village on the border between the two Koreas.
fact: The Demilitarized Zone is about 4 km wide and 250 km long.

name: Mount Fuji, Japan
clues: A perfect white cone that the painters adore, / they climb me by night for the sunrise in store.
I'm a volcano, a goddess and a symbol of my country, and I'm open to climbers only in summer. What am I?
A snow-capped volcano and the tallest peak in Japan.
fact: Mount Fuji is 3,776 m tall, and the official climbing season lasts only about two months each summer.

name: Malé, Maldives
clues: A city that covers its island in full, / where the sea's at the door and the streets are packed full.
I'm one of the most crowded capitals on Earth, and the highest ground in my country is just a few meters up. What am I?
The capital of an island nation in the Indian Ocean.
fact: The Maldives is the flattest country in the world.

name: Brandenburg Gate, Berlin, Germany
clues: A chariot of horses rides high on my top, / where a wall once said that all crossing must stop.
I'm a gate that was shut for 28 years, and now anyone can walk through me. What am I?
The famous gate in the heart of Berlin.
fact: The Berlin Wall ran right beside the Brandenburg Gate from 1961 to 1989.

name: Wieliczka Salt Mine, Poland
clues: Chapels and statues carved deep in the earth, / all made of salt, for whatever that's worth.
Miners carved a cathedral here, and you can lick the walls. What am I?
An old salt mine near Kraków.
fact: Salt was mined at Wieliczka from the 13th century until 1996.

name: Angkor Wat, Cambodia
clues: The largest of temples, reflected in pools, / five lotus towers where the jungle rules.
I'm on my country's flag, and the sun rises right behind my towers twice a year. What am I?
Angkor Wat temple in Cambodia.
fact: Angkor Wat faces west, which is unusual for a temple of its kind, and the sun rises right behind its towers at the equinox.

name: Dead Sea
clues: You can't sink in me, though try as you might, / you float on my water and read in the light.
I'm called a sea but I'm a lake, I'm the lowest place on land, and nothing much can live in me. What am I?
A lake so salty it is called 'dead'.
fact: The Dead Sea's shore is about 430 m below sea level and the water level drops about 1 m a year.

name: Hampi, India
clues: Boulders are balanced like toys on the plain, / where a kingdom once glittered, now ruins remain.
My stone chariot never moved, but you'll find it on my country's money. What am I?
The ruins of the Vijayanagara capital in Karnataka.
fact: Hampi's stone chariot at the Vittala Temple appears on India's 50-rupee note.

name: Kirkjufell, Iceland
clues: A church made of mountain, an arrowhead cone, / with waterfalls posing in front of my stone.
I'm a mountain shaped like a witch's hat, and I starred in a TV fantasy about dragons. What am I?
A cone-shaped mountain on Iceland's Snæfellsnes peninsula.
fact: Kirkjufell means 'church mountain'.

name: Badwater Basin, Death Valley, USA
clues: The lowest of all, in a valley of heat, / salt hexagons crunch under travelers' feet.
I'm the lowest point in North America, yet the highest peak in the lower 48 states is close by. What am I?
A salt flat in Death Valley, California.
fact: Mount Whitney, the highest point in the lower 48 states, is less than 140 km from Badwater.

name: Tiger's Nest Monastery, Bhutan
clues: Hanging on cliffs where a tiger once flew, / a guru on its back, the monks say it's true.
Legend says a tigress carried a holy man to this cliff, and now I'm a monastery that seems to float. What am I?
Paro Taktsang, a monastery in Bhutan.
fact: Bhutan measures its progress with Gross National Happiness.

name: Victoria Falls, Zambia and Zimbabwe
clues: The smoke that thunders, the locals say, / you'll feel my mist from miles away.
I'm the largest curtain of falling water, and in the dry season you can swim right on my edge. What am I?
Victoria Falls on the Zambezi River.
fact: At full flood, more than 500 million liters of water per minute pour over Victoria Falls.

name: Lalibela, Ethiopia
clues: Churches cut down into rock, not built high, / an African Jerusalem under the sky.
My churches were never built, they were carved downward, one stone block each. What am I?
Rock-hewn churches in the Ethiopian highlands.
fact: Lalibela's 11 churches were carved around the 12th and 13th centuries and are still used for worship.

name: Svalbard (Longyearbyen), Norway
clues: Polar bears outnumber the people out here, / the sun doesn't set for months of the year.
Dying is officially discouraged in my town, and the world's backup seeds are stored in my mountain. What am I?
Longyearbyen, the main town of Svalbard.
fact: The Global Seed Vault holds more than a million seed samples from almost every country.

name: Times Square, New York City
clues: My lights never sleep and my billboards shine bright, / at midnight on New Year a ball falls in sight.
I'm named after a newspaper, and I'm called the crossroads of the world. What am I?
Times Square, Manhattan.
fact: The New Year's Eve ball drop in Times Square started in 1907.

name: Shibuya Crossing, Tokyo, Japan
clues: When lights all turn green, a thousand feet stride, / while a loyal bronze dog keeps waiting outside.
I'm the busiest pedestrian crossing in the world, and my most famous resident is a bronze dog. What am I?
The world's busiest pedestrian crossing, in Tokyo.
fact: The dog Hachikō waited at Shibuya Station for his owner every day for nearly ten years.

name: Preikestolen, Norway
clues: A flat stone pulpit hung high on a fjord, / step close to my edge, but you'll never be bored.
My name means preacher's pulpit, and I'm a cliff 600 m above the water. What am I?
A cliff above the Lysefjord in Norway.
fact: About 300,000 people hike to Preikestolen each year.

name: Alhambra, Granada, Spain
clues: Red castle of patterns and fountains that play, / the last Moorish kings had to give me away.
My name means the red one, and my walls are covered in poetry. What am I?
A Moorish palace above Granada.
fact: The Alhambra was the last stronghold of Muslim rule in Spain, until 1492.

name: Torres del Paine, Chile
clues: Three granite horns in a land of blue ice, / the wind there is wild, so pack something nice.
My towers are made of granite, and my name might mean blue in a local language. What am I?
A national park in Chilean Patagonia.
fact: 'Paine' is thought to mean 'blue' in the local Tehuelche language.

name: Registan, Samarkand, Uzbekistan
clues: Three blue-tiled schools on a sandy square, / on the Silk Road where the caravans fare.
My name means sandy place, but I'm covered in blue tiles and gold. What am I?
The famous square of Samarkand.
fact: Registan means 'sandy place' in Persian.

name: Komodo Island, Indonesia
clues: Dragons are real here, they swim and they roam, / with a bite full of venom they guard their home.
I'm named after real dragons, but they can't fly or breathe fire. What am I?
An island in the Lesser Sunda chain, home of dragons.
fact: Komodo dragons can grow to 3 m long.

name: Tikal, Guatemala
clues: Temples poke out of a jungle so deep, / where howler monkeys won't let you sleep.
I played a rebel base in a famous space movie, but I was really a Maya city. What am I?
A great Maya city in the jungle of northern Guatemala.
fact: Tikal appeared as the Rebel base on Yavin 4 in the first Star Wars film in 1977.

name: Ilulissat Icefjord, Greenland
clues: Icebergs as tall as skyscrapers float, / born from a glacier, too big for a boat.
One of my glacier's icebergs may have sunk the Titanic. What am I?
An icefjord on Greenland's west coast.
fact: Sermeq Kujalleq glacier produces about 10% of Greenland's icebergs.

name: Colosseum, Rome, Italy
clues: Gladiators fought where tourists now throng, / my seats held fifty thousand who cheered all day long.
I lost stones to build a church, and I'm broken on one side, but I'm still a giant. What am I?
The great amphitheater of the Roman emperors.
fact: Much of the Colosseum's missing stone was taken to build other buildings in Rome, including St Peter's.

name: Ushuaia, Argentina
clues: The end of the world is what people call me, / a prison once built me beside a cold sea.
I'm called the southernmost city in the world, and many ships leave me for Antarctica. What am I?
The southernmost city on the island of Tierra del Fuego.
fact: Ushuaia was founded around a prison, which is now a museum.

name: Borobudur, Indonesia
clues: A mountain of stone with stupas like bells, / a Buddha in each, and a story it tells.
I'm the largest Buddhist temple on Earth, hidden for centuries under volcanic ash and jungle. What am I?
The largest Buddhist temple in the world, on the island of Java.
fact: Borobudur was built in the 9th century from about two million stone blocks.

name: Havana, Cuba
clues: Old cars in candy colors cruise by the sea, / cigars and salsa, come dance with me.
My streets are full of 1950s cars, and my seawall is the city's living room. What am I?
The capital of Cuba.
fact: Old Havana and its fortifications became a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1982.

name: Table Mountain, Cape Town, South Africa
clues: A mountain so flat that a tablecloth lies / of cloud on my top in the summer skies.
A constellation in the sky was named after me, and a cable car spins as it climbs me. What am I?
The flat-topped mountain above Cape Town.
fact: The constellation Mensa, 'the table', was named after Table Mountain in the 1750s.

name: Angel Falls, Venezuela
clues: The tallest of falls from a mountain of stone, / named for a pilot whose plane got stuck on its throne.
I'm named after a pilot, not a heavenly being, and my water turns to mist before it lands. What am I?
The world's tallest waterfall, in Venezuela.
fact: Angel Falls drops 979 m, with an unbroken fall of 807 m.

name: Dubrovnik, Croatia
clues: My walls wrap the city in old stone embrace, / a king's landing in a fantasy place.
I'm called the pearl of my sea, and dragons flew over my walls on TV. What am I?
A walled old town on the Adriatic coast.
fact: Dubrovnik's walls are nearly 2 km around and up to 25 m high.

name: Thingvellir, Iceland
clues: Two continents split here, the crack growing wide, / you can dive in between them, one on each side.
I'm where the world's oldest parliament met in the open air, between two plates of Earth. What am I?
Thingvellir (Þingvellir), Iceland.
fact: The rift valley at Thingvellir widens by about 2 cm every year.

name: Cartagena, Colombia
clues: Walls round my old town with balconies bright, / colorful streets on the Caribbean night.
Pirates once attacked me so often that my people built walls 11 km long. What am I?
A walled Caribbean port city in Colombia.
fact: Cartagena's city walls stretch about 11 km.

name: Lake Titicaca, Peru and Bolivia
clues: High in the mountains, the highest that sails, / with islands of reeds that float in my tales.
I'm a lake shared by two countries, so high that boats can sail almost 4 km above the sea. What am I?
The highest navigable lake in the world, between Peru and Bolivia.
fact: Lake Titicaca sits about 3,812 m above sea level.

name: Chefchaouen, Morocco
clues: Every wall is painted in shades of blue, / in a town in the mountains, the sky looks through.
My whole town is painted blue, and no one agrees on why. What am I?
The blue city of northern Morocco.
fact: Chefchaouen was founded in 1471 as a small fortress.

name: Great Barrier Reef, Australia
clues: The largest living thing, seen from the sky, / made of tiny animals, glowing nearby.
I'm made of billions of tiny animals, and I'm longer than Italy. What am I?
The giant coral reef off Queensland.
fact: The Great Barrier Reef is made of about 2,900 individual reefs.

name: Pompeii, Italy
clues: Buried in ash in a day and a night, / my people were frozen in shapes of their fright.
A mountain swallowed me in a day, and that's why I'm one of the best preserved cities of my age. What am I?
A Roman town at the foot of Mount Vesuvius.
fact: Pompeii was rediscovered in the 1700s, about 1,600 years after it was buried.

name: Moraine Lake, Canada
clues: Turquoise as paint under ten jagged peaks, / I'm frozen for most of the year, many weeks.
My water is so blue it was on a banknote, and my color comes from ground-up rock. What am I?
A glacier lake below ten peaks in Banff National Park.
fact: Moraine Lake is usually frozen until June.

name: Las Vegas Strip, USA
clues: My nights are brighter than days ever seem, / a pyramid shoots out a heavenly beam.
I have a pyramid, the Eiffel Tower and Venice, but I'm in the desert. What am I?
The neon street of casinos in Nevada.
fact: The beam of light from the top of the Luxor pyramid is among the strongest in the world.

name: St Basil's Cathedral, Moscow, Russia
clues: Nine candy-striped onions crown my red square, / a legend says my builder was blinded right there.
I look like I came from a fairy tale, but I was built to celebrate a war victory. What am I?
The colorful cathedral on Red Square.
fact: St Basil's was built in the 1550s to celebrate a military victory by Ivan the Terrible.

name: Forbidden City, Beijing, China
clues: Nine thousand rooms behind walls of deep red, / for five hundred years only emperors tread.
I was called forbidden, yet millions of visitors walk through my gates every year. What am I?
The imperial palace in the heart of Beijing.
fact: The Forbidden City was home to 24 emperors of the Ming and Qing dynasties.

name: Arctic Circle, Rovaniemi, Finland
clues: Step over my line and the sun may not set, / a man in red reads every letter you get.
Children all over the world send me letters, and reindeer are my neighbors. What am I?
Santa Claus Village on the Arctic Circle in Finland.
fact: Santa's main post office in Rovaniemi gets letters from about 200 countries.

name: Mount Everest
clues: I'm the roof of the world, and I'm growing still, / my top is a border on the highest hill.
I'm the highest place on Earth, yet people have left their trash on me. What am I?
The highest point on Earth above sea level.
fact: The summit of Everest is made of marine limestone. It was once the floor of an ancient sea.

name: Burj Khalifa, Dubai, UAE
clues: A silver needle sewn into the sky, / you can watch the sun set twice if you ride up high.
I'm the tallest building ever, and my top sways a little in the desert wind. What am I?
The tallest building in the world, in Dubai.
fact: The Burj Khalifa is 828 m tall and opened in 2010.

name: Hiroshima Peace Memorial, Japan
clues: My dome is a skeleton, kept as it stood, / so the world won't forget, and it never should.
I survived the blast that destroyed my city, and paper cranes are folded for me. What am I?
The A-Bomb Dome in Hiroshima.
fact: The dome was one of the few buildings left standing near the hypocenter on 6 August 1945.

name: Amsterdam, Netherlands
clues: On bikes and on boats all my people commute, / my houses lean over canals, tall and cute.
My canals ring the old town like half-moons, and millions visit a hidden annex where a girl wrote her diary. What am I?
The Dutch capital of canals.
fact: Amsterdam's 17th-century canal ring is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

name: Big Ben, London, England
clues: My bell has a name that the world calls me, / but my real name is a queen's, as you'll see.
People call me by my bell's name, and my four faces keep a country on time. What am I?
The clock tower at the Houses of Parliament in London.
fact: The tower was renamed Elizabeth Tower in 2012 for Queen Elizabeth II's Diamond Jubilee.

name: Avenue of the Baobabs, Madagascar
clues: Upside-down trees with their roots in the sky, / we line a red road as the sunset goes by.
We're trees that store water in our trunks, on an island where lemurs live and nowhere else. What am I?
A road of giant baobab trees near Morondava.
fact: Six of the world's eight baobab species grow only in Madagascar.

name: Socotra, Yemen
clues: Umbrella trees bleeding a dragon's red blood, / on an island that time left alone in the mud.
A third of my plants grow nowhere else on Earth, and my trees look like they're from another planet. What am I?
Socotra island, part of Yemen.
fact: The red resin of Socotra's dragon's blood tree has been traded since ancient times as dye and medicine.

name: Alcatraz, San Francisco, USA
clues: They called me the Rock, and the sea was my guard, / three men on a raft may have slipped out my yard.
Al Capone slept here, and the cold currents kept everyone in. What am I?
The prison island in San Francisco Bay.
fact: Alcatraz was a federal prison from 1934 to 1963. Al Capone was one of its inmates.

name: Niagara Falls, Canada and USA
clues: Three curtains of water that never will close, / where daredevils tumbled in barrels, and rose.
I'm shared by two countries, and honeymooners take boats right into my mist. What am I?
Three waterfalls on the border between Ontario and New York.
fact: Annie Edson Taylor was the first person to survive going over Niagara Falls in a barrel.

name: Grand Canyon, Arizona, USA
clues: Two billion years of Earth's diary I keep, / a river wrote every page, a mile deep.
I was carved by a river that's still at my bottom, and you can walk out over me on a glass horseshoe. What am I?
A mile-deep canyon cut by the Colorado River in Arizona.
fact: The Grand Canyon is about 446 km long and up to 29 km wide.

name: Meeting of the Waters, Manaus, Brazil
clues: Coffee and milk flowing side by side, / two rivers that meet but refuse to collide.
I'm where a black river and a sandy one meet and don't mix for miles. What am I?
Where the Rio Negro meets the Amazon, in Brazil.
fact: The two rivers differ in temperature, speed and density, which keeps them apart.

name: Teotihuacan, Mexico
clues: The city of gods was in ruins when found, / by the Aztecs who named it, and walked on its ground.
My Avenue of the Dead leads from a pyramid of the Sun to a pyramid of the Moon. What am I?
The Pyramids of the Sun and Moon, near Mexico City.
fact: At its peak around 500 AD, Teotihuacan may have had more than 100,000 people.

name: Galapagos Islands, Ecuador
clues: Giant tortoises older than grandparents roam, / and a famous young scientist made me his home.
My finches helped change science forever, and my iguanas swim in the sea. What am I?
The Galapagos Islands, part of Ecuador.
fact: Galapagos giant tortoises can live for more than 100 years.

name: Neuschwanstein Castle, Germany
clues: A king built me for dreams, and died before done, / now a mouse's castle has copied my fun.
I look like a fairy tale, but I was built only about 150 years ago, in the Alps. What am I?
A fairy-tale castle in the Bavarian Alps.
fact: King Ludwig II of Bavaria died in 1886, before Neuschwanstein was finished.

name: Atomium, Brussels, Belgium
clues: Nine silver balls that are built like a cell, / of iron blown up, where you can walk as well.
I'm a giant model of something too small to see, and I was built for a World's Fair. What am I?
Nine giant silver balls in Brussels.
fact: The Atomium is 102 m tall, and you can ride an escalator between its spheres.

name: Salar de Uyuni, Bolivia
clues: After the rain I'm the world's biggest mirror, / where earth meets the sky, nothing could be clearer.
I'm a white desert of salt, and satellites use me to check their measurements. What am I?
The biggest salt flat in the world, high in the Andes of Bolivia.
fact: Salar de Uyuni covers more than 10,000 square kilometers and varies in height by less than a meter.

name: McMurdo Station, Antarctica
clues: The biggest town on the continent of ice, / where summer's still freezing, and penguins are nice.
I'm a town with a church, a harbor and a runway made of ice. What am I?
The main US research base in Antarctica.
fact: McMurdo can house about 1,000 people in the summer.

name: San Pedro de Atacama, Chile
clues: The driest of deserts surrounds my oasis, / with geysers and moon valleys, wonderful places.
Some of my neighbors have never seen rain, and NASA tests Mars rovers near me. What am I?
An oasis town in the driest non-polar desert on Earth.
fact: The Atacama is so dry and clear that it hosts some of the world's largest telescopes.

name: Hallstatt, Austria
clues: A village so pretty that China built two, / squeezed by a lake and the mountains, it's true.
My village is so lovely it was copied house by house, and I have one of the oldest salt mines on Earth. What am I?
A lakeside village in the Austrian Alps.
fact: Hallstatt's bone house holds hundreds of painted skulls, because the tiny graveyard ran out of space.

name: Ha Long Bay, Vietnam
clues: A dragon came down and spat jewels in the sea, / now thousands of islands rise up, wild and free.
I'm a bay of nearly 2,000 limestone islands, and my name means descending dragon. What am I?
A bay of green islands in northern Vietnam.
fact: Ha Long means 'descending dragon' in Vietnamese.

name: Belém Tower, Lisbon, Portugal
clues: A rhinoceros carved on my riverside wall, / I waved explorers goodbye, one and all.
I'm a fortress that looks like a chess piece, guarding the river where explorers set sail. What am I?
A riverside fortress at the mouth of the Tagus in Lisbon.
fact: The rhino carving is thought to show the rhinoceros sent to Lisbon from India in 1515.

name: Hagia Sophia, Istanbul, Türkiye
clues: A church, then a mosque, then a museum, then more, / my dome seems to float on light, as before.
For nearly a thousand years I was the largest cathedral on Earth, on the line between two continents. What am I?
The great domed building of old Constantinople.
fact: Hagia Sophia's main dome rises about 55 m above the floor.

name: Persepolis, Iran
clues: Winged bulls guard my gate that says All Nations, / a conqueror burned me after his celebrations.
Kings of kings received gifts from every land on my staircases. What am I?
The ceremonial capital of the ancient Persian Empire.
fact: Persepolis was founded by Darius the Great around 518 BC.

name: Oia, Santorini, Greece
clues: Sugar-cube houses and domes made of sky, / on a sunken volcano's rim, perched up high.
Every evening crowds gather here just to clap for the sunset. What am I?
White houses and blue domes on a Greek island in the Aegean.
fact: The Minoan eruption of Santorini was one of the largest volcanic eruptions in human history.

name: Sydney Opera House, Australia
clues: Sails that don't sail, or shells by the sea, / a million white tiles make a roof out of me.
My architect cut my shells like slices of an orange, and he never saw me finished. What am I?
White sails on a harbour, near a famous bridge nicknamed the Coathanger.
fact: Danish architect Jørn Utzon resigned in 1966 and never returned to see the finished building.

name: Göreme, Cappadocia, Türkiye
clues: My chimneys are rocks where the fairies once dwelled, / with balloons in the sky at sunrise propelled.
Whole cities are hidden under me, and churches are carved inside my rocks. What am I?
The land of fairy chimneys in central Türkiye.
fact: Derinkuyu, an underground city nearby, goes down about 85 m and could shelter thousands.

name: Hobbiton, Matamata, New Zealand
clues: Round little doors in a green rolling hill, / no hobbit lives here, but tourists come still.
I'm a village of small round doors on a sheep farm, and no one has ever lived here. What am I?
The hobbit village film set on New Zealand's North Island.
fact: Hobbiton was rebuilt in permanent materials for The Hobbit films and is now a tourist attraction.

name: Pyramids of Meroë, Sudan
clues: Steep pyramids standing, more than Egypt's own, / but few people visit my desert of stone.
I was the royal city of black pharaohs and warrior queens, along the Nile. What am I?
The royal pyramids of ancient Kush, in Sudan.
fact: In the 1830s an Italian treasure hunter blew the tops off dozens of Meroë's pyramids looking for gold.

name: Petronas Towers, Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia
clues: Twin towers of steel holding hands in the air, / a bridge at the middle, we're a matching pair.
We're twins, but built by two different companies racing each other. What am I?
Malaysia's famous twin skyscrapers.
fact: The Petronas Towers were the tallest buildings in the world from 1998 to 2004.

name: Timbuktu, Mali
clues: People think I'm a myth at the end of the earth, / but my mud mosques kept scholars' books of great worth.
My name became a word for the middle of nowhere, but I'm a real city. What am I?
A legendary desert city in Mali whose name starts with 'Tim'.
fact: Timbuktu's Djinguereber Mosque was built around 1327 and is still made of mud brick.

name: Monaco
clues: Smaller than a park, with a prince and a throne, / race cars scream through my streets and my stone.
I'm the second smallest country, with no farms at all but plenty of yachts. What am I?
A tiny principality on the French Riviera.
fact: Monaco is the second-smallest country in the world after Vatican City.

name: Fushimi Inari Shrine, Kyoto, Japan
clues: Ten thousand orange gates climb up my hill, / and stone foxes guard them, sitting quite still.
I'm a path through thousands of gates, each one a gift from a business hoping for luck. What am I?
Fushimi Inari shrine in Kyoto.
fact: The paths of torii gates at Fushimi Inari wind about 4 km up Mount Inari.

name: Jemaa el-Fnaa, Marrakech, Morocco
clues: Snake charmers by day, a kitchen by night, / my square in the Red City buzzes with light.
My name might mean assembly of the dead, but I'm the liveliest square in Africa. What am I?
The great square of Morocco's Red City.
fact: The square was one of the first places on UNESCO's list of Masterpieces of the Oral and Intangible Heritage of Humanity in 2001.

name: Panama Canal, Panama
clues: Ships climb up stairs made of water and locks, / two oceans meet here between my stone docks.
I'm a shortcut between two oceans, and ships sail through me going southeast to get from the Atlantic to the Pacific. What am I?
The canal across a narrow Central American country.
fact: Each ship passing through the Panama Canal uses about 200 million liters of fresh water from Gatun Lake.

name: The South Pole
clues: Every way north from the place where I stand, / you can circle the world in one step on my land.
From here, every direction is north, and my marker has to be moved about ten meters every year. What am I?
The southern end of Earth's axis.
fact: The ice at the South Pole moves about 10 m a year, so the marker for the exact pole is moved every January.

name: Half Dome, Yosemite, USA
clues: Half of a dome cut clean down the face, / climbers pull up my back on cables in place.
I look like I was sliced in half, and I'm the logo of an outdoor clothing brand. What am I?
A granite dome in Yosemite National Park, California.
fact: Half Dome rises about 1,444 m above the floor of Yosemite Valley.

name: Lake Bled, Slovenia
clues: An island with a church in a lake green and bright, / ring my bell for a wish, climb 99 steps right.
I'm the only island in my country, and grooms carry brides up my steps. What am I?
An alpine lake with a church on an island, in Slovenia.
fact: Bled's island is the only natural island in Slovenia.

name: Sigiriya, Sri Lanka
clues: A king built his palace on top of a stone, / and you enter through lion's paws, on your own.
I'm a rock fortress in the jungle with ancient graffiti and a mirror wall. What am I?
The Lion Rock fortress in Sri Lanka.
fact: Sigiriya was built by King Kashyapa in the 5th century.

name: Marina Bay Sands, Singapore
clues: Three towers that carry a ship on their heads, / with a pool at the edge, where the city spreads.
I'm a hotel with a boat on my roof, next to a garden of giant metal trees. What am I?
A famous hotel on the waterfront of a city-state.
fact: Singapore is one of only three surviving city-states.

name: Icehotel, Jukkasjärvi, Sweden
clues: Rebuilt every winter, I melt in the spring, / my beds and my glasses are a frozen thing.
I'm made from river ice, and every year I'm designed by different artists. What am I?
A hotel made of ice in Swedish Lapland.
fact: The first Icehotel was built in 1989-90 on the Torne River.

name: Maya Bay, Thailand
clues: A movie made me so famous, it's true, / I had to close down to let nature renew.
I'm a beach so loved by visitors that I had to be closed for years. What am I?
A cove on Ko Phi Phi Le in the Andaman Sea.
fact: Maya Bay was closed from 2018 to 2022 to let its coral and sharks recover.

name: Mount Rushmore, USA
clues: Four faces of stone, sixty feet tall, / we never blink, we see it all.
We're four presidents carved into a mountain sacred to the Lakota. What am I?
Four presidents carved into a mountain in South Dakota.
fact: Carving Mount Rushmore took 14 years, from 1927 to 1941, mostly with dynamite.

name: Point Nemo, South Pacific
clues: The farthest from land that a sailor can be, / old spaceships come down here to rest in the sea.
Often the closest people to me are astronauts in space. What am I?
The 'oceanic pole of inaccessibility', named after Jules Verne's submarine captain.
fact: The nearest land to Point Nemo is about 2,700 km away.

name: The Bund, Shanghai, China
clues: Old banks in a row by a river that bends, / face a forest of towers where the skyline ascends.
My old buildings look at a future skyline across the river. What am I?
Shanghai's famous waterfront.
fact: The Shanghai Tower across the river is the tallest building in China.

name: Potala Palace, Lhasa, Tibet
clues: A thousand rooms climbing a red-and-white hill, / the roof of the world, standing proud and still.
I was the winter palace of the Dalai Lamas, and white means living while red means praying. What am I?
A red-and-white palace in Lhasa.
fact: The Potala Palace is 13 stories tall and was built in the 1600s on an older site.

name: Abu Simbel, Egypt
clues: Four giant kings sitting tall by the Nile, / were cut up and moved, to stay dry for a while.
Twice a year the sun reaches deep inside me and lights up the faces of the gods. What am I?
Giant statues of Ramesses II near the Sudan border.
fact: Moving Abu Simbel took four years and a global campaign led by UNESCO.

name: Eiffel Tower, Paris, France
clues: Meant to be scrapped, I was built for a fair, / I grow in the summer, and sparkle in air.
I have four feet but never walk, I wear lace you can't remove, and I sparkle every hour after dark. What am I?
The iron lady on the Champ de Mars.
fact: The Eiffel Tower grows about 15 cm taller in summer as the iron expands in the heat.
